title: Gluten Free Banana Bread Waffles
description: The softest 4 ingredient gluten free and sugar free banana bread waffle sticks. Ready in just 10 minutes, these waffles are perfect for when you want banana bread without any of the effort.

hero.alt: A hand holding a gluten free banana bread waffle stick with white chocolate dripping down and a banana slice on top

thumbnail.alt: A hand holding a gluten free banana bread waffle stick with white chocolate dripping down and a banana slice on top

instructions.text: Preheat your waffle maker per its instructions. If making pancakes instead, heat a pan on low to medium heat and add a little oil if needed.
In a bowl, mash the bananas well. Add in the eggs and cinnamon and mix until combined.
Stir in the baking powder and cassava flour. The batter will be on the runnier side.
Add a few teaspoons of batter to your waffle maker or pan. Cook for approximately 2 minutes on each side until lightly golden.
Let them cool slightly and enjoy!

notes: Use very overripe bananas with lots of brown spots for maximum sweetness and flavour.
Let the waffles cook fully before opening the waffle iron to prevent sticking.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for 2 to 3 days. Reheat in the toaster or oven for the best texture.
Can also be frozen. Let cool completely, freeze in an airtight container, then reheat in a toaster or oven.

story.subtitle: 4 ingredient, sugar free and gluten free
paragraphs: if you love banana bread but don't love the time and process it takes to make it, you will be obsessed with these 4 ingredient banana bread waffles. not only are they the perfect use of any overripe bananas sitting on your counter but they will become a permanent fixture in your breakfast rotation too! they taste just like classic banana bread but take half the time and you only need four healthy ingredients.

these gluten free banana bread waffles are naturally sweetened with ripe bananas, completely added sugar free, and made with cassava flour for the perfect soft and fluffy texture. cassava flour is made from the whole root of the cassava plant and has a naturally neutral flavour that works really well in a lot of bakes. it is very absorbent and acts differently to regular gluten flour but it still gives you a soft and moist crumb without the graininess you can get with other gluten free flours. the texture is really reminiscent of a classic banana bread loaf but extra soft.

one thing i love about bananas as a sweetener is that they bring so much more than just sweetness. they add natural moisture to the batter, contribute potassium and vitamin B6, and help create that soft, tender interior. the more spotted and overripe your bananas are, the sweeter and more flavourful your waffles will be, so this is really one of the best uses for bananas that have gone past the point of eating fresh.

these are perfect for busy mornings since the batter comes together in under 10 minutes and the waffles cook quickly. they also store well in the fridge and reheat beautifully in the toaster or oven on low heat, so you can make a batch at the weekend and enjoy them during the week. feeling more banana bread goodness? your next bake should be my chocolate chip banana bread bars.

cinnamon note: i always use ceylon cinnamon instead of cassia. there are several reasons for this but the most important to know is that cassia cinnamon can become toxic if consumed too frequently in large amounts and since i am a massive cinnamon lover i always go heavy handed with it and add it to all my autumn or cozy bakes.

the actual science behind this comes down to a compound found in cinnamon called coumarin. it is 250 times higher in cassia cinnamon vs ceylon cinnamon. the effects of this compound are quite varied ranging from liver toxicity, interactions with medication to gastrointestinal discomfort. whereas, ceylon cinnamon only contains trace amounts of coumarin and has several health benefits such as improved glycemic control, high polyphenol count, antimicrobial functions and cardiovascular support. so feel free to go heavy handed with the ceylon cinnamon!

the waffle maker is the main component of this recipe and is what makes it so much faster than baking a loaf of banana bread. if you have never tried waffle sticks before, you are in for a treat, not only are they so cute but the size means you get the perfect touch of crisp textures and soft centers which is basically the best part of banana bread. and each waffle stick only takes a couple of minutes to cook! if you don't have a waffle stick maker, a regular waffle iron works just as well.

a properly preheated waffle iron is key here and what makes the waffle sticks cook without getting stuck but also achieving those golden crisp edges. most waffle irons have an indicator light that tells you when they're ready but as a rough guide i let mine cook for 2 minutes on each side. ensure you lightly grease the iron before and between each waffle even if it says the iron is non-stick, because the banana batter has a slightly higher natural sugar content that can caramelise and stick to even a non-stick surface.

turning these into waffle sticks is such a fun idea for kids, for grabbing on the go, or just because they're so much easier to dip than a full waffle! once the waffles are done, let them cool slightly. you can enjoy them still warm and freshly baked or store them and reheat in the toaster for your next sweet snack or meal prepped breakfast. they're perfect for dipping into your fave nut butter, even a small bowl of melted dark chocolate for an indulgent moment or just eating them as is!

faq.question: Are these banana bread waffles gluten free?
faq.answer: Yes, these waffles are made with cassava flour, which is naturally gluten free and grain free. Unlike some gluten free flour blends, cassava flour is also paleo friendly. Make sure the baking powder you use is also gluten free if you are strictly avoiding gluten.

faq.question: How do I store waffle sticks?
faq.answer: Store these banana bread waffle sticks in an airtight container in the fridge for 2 to 3 days. Reheat in the toaster or oven for the best eating experience. They can also be frozen in a single layer, then transferred to a freezer bag for up to 1 month. Reheat from frozen in the toaster or oven until warmed through and lightly golden again.

faq.question: Are these banana bread waffles sugar free?
faq.answer: These waffles contain no added sugar. The sweetness comes naturally from overripe bananas, which makes them added sugar free and refined sugar free. Bananas do contain naturally occurring fruit sugars, but no sweetener is added to the batter itself.

faq.question: Can I substitute cassava flour?
faq.answer: Cassava flour works best for the soft, fluffy texture in this recipe. A 1:1 gluten free flour blend is the closest substitute, though the texture may vary slightly depending on the blend. I haven't tested this substitution myself, so I'd recommend sticking with cassava flour for the best results.

faq.question: Can I make dairy free banana bread waffles?
faq.answer: Yes, this recipe is naturally dairy free. There is no butter or dairy-based ingredients in the batter. You can top with any dairy free drizzle such as maple syrup or your dairy free chocolate of choice.

faq.question: Can I freeze banana bread waffles?
faq.answer: Yes. Let them cool completely after cooking, then freeze in a single layer on a tray before transferring to a freezer safe container or bag. To reheat, pop them straight into the toaster or oven from frozen and heat until warmed through and slightly crispy. They come out almost as good as fresh.

faq.question: Why are my waffles sticking to the waffle maker?
faq.answer: Make sure your waffle iron is fully preheated before adding the batter, as adding batter to a cold or only partially heated iron is the most common cause of sticking. Lightly grease the plates with cooking spray or a thin wipe of oil before each batch. Also let the waffles cook fully without opening the iron early: the waffle will release naturally from the plates once it is properly cooked and lightly golden.

faq.question: Can I make these into pancakes instead of waffles?
faq.answer: Yes, absolutely. The same batter works really well as fluffy pancakes. Heat a non-stick pan on medium-low heat and add a small amount of oil or cooking spray. Pour small portions of batter and cook for about 2 minutes until the surface starts to bubble, then flip and cook for another 1 to 2 minutes. They come out soft, fluffy, and delicious.

tips: Use very overripe bananas with lots of brown spots. The more ripe they are, the sweeter and more flavourful your waffles will be without needing any added sugar.
Let the waffles cook fully before opening the waffle iron. They need time to set and will stick if you open the iron too early. Wait for the steam to reduce before checking.
The batter is on the runnier side, which is normal for this recipe. Don't be tempted to add more flour as the texture loosens up beautifully once cooked.
Reheat leftovers in the toaster or oven rather than the microwave. The toaster restores the golden, slightly crisp exterior that makes these so satisfying.

alternatives: 1:1 gluten free flour blend (texture may vary slightly)
Arrowroot flour can work in a smaller quantity
Frozen and thawed bananas work great and are often sweeter
Use the ripest bananas possible for best natural sweetness
Flax eggs may work for a vegan version though texture will differ
This recipe has only been tested with regular eggs
